property_summary: For any caller address newOwner, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) on the correct contract always reverts when newOwner == address(0) (preventing setting owner to zero), but the mutant allows the owner to become the zero address for some inputs (it replaces the non-zero requirement with a redundant owner check), so the property is violated for some fuzzed newOwner values of zero.
change_summary: Require newOwner not zero removed and replaced with requiring caller be current owner (redundant but changes behavior when owner check differs); emits OwnershipTransferred unchanged — this allows transferOwnership to succeed even if newOwner is zero when called by owner? Actually replaces the non-zero check with an explicit onlyOwner invocation inside function body, changing revert condition source.
